briefHtml:
NAV S$10,368,633 — slight uptick (watcher −0.154%; ≈+0.06% vs the restated Sep 25 base) · listed flag −0.825% · zero riskFlags (6th consecutive clean day) · Sep 25 restated −S$8.2k (three nights: ~S$39k)

  • Biggest mover: the relief bounce. WTI −2.33% to $92.41 (−7.4% w/w) after Iran proposed reopening Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks within 7 days (conditions: lift the blockade, unfreeze assets, end the war on all fronts — a June-MOU-style sequence). Miners bounced: SILJ +1.00% to $29.22, GDX +0.56% to $92.87, SLV +0.90% (silver est ~$64.3 — 4th defense of the $62–64 zone), GLD +0.44% (gold est ~$4,315). US rallied (Dow +0.93%, S&P +0.51% to 7,743.41) and the 10y eased 4bp to 5.17%. Exception: HK sold −1.01% on a holiday-thinned tape; Tencent closed below the 439 tell a second session (HK$436.60); Xiaomi −2.56%.
  • The one thing: the summit scorecard is out. Beijing's eight outcomes: strategic-stability framing; APEC/G20 mutual attendance; Iran no-nukes + no transit fees in international waterways; Trade Council + $30bn reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement; fentanyl scheduling; the 'U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue' — next exchange by November 2026, plus an SI-incident channel; pandas to Atlanta. WH extras: at least 10Mt/yr US coal 2027–28, a refined-petroleum production ask, a Board of Investment, only aspirational rare-earths language. Mil-mil crisis-communication MoU to be signed ASAP. NOT landed: Taiwan absent from the outcomes; rare-earth flows still falling. This week: RBA Tue (~96% priced hike), US PCE Wed, EZ CPI + NFP Fri.

Risk flags — none

  • riskFlags empty, 6th day · silver est +0.9% Friday · L46.SI Yahoo 404, 12th session · SLVP frozen a 3rd session (Friday close not captured) · VIX 14.87 −5.11% (Google late print)
  • Silver line (est): 1,777 oz × ~$64.3 × 1.2787 ≈ S$146.1k vs S$56.24k loan ≈ 1.63x → equity ≈ S$89.9k, +1.5% day-recovery from Thursday's ~S$88.6k
  • Tell status: Tencent two closes below 439 on thin volume — today is the first full-flow test (mainland back, scorecard known); reclaim 439 with volume = tranche trigger; failure toward 425 = wait
  • Rates: 10y 5.17% off the 5.21% peak but October-hike odds ~66%; Bessent buybacks seen as having limited impact; PCE Wed + NFP Fri are the gauntlet; Norges hiked to 4.50%, Riksbank hawkish-hold, Banxico outcome not explicitly captured
  • Iran: 7-day proposal live but the June MOU precedent says it can collapse; WTI −7.4% w/w; Hormuz flows ~33.7M bbl, on track with prior week
  • Quirks/gaps: third straight restatement (~S$39k across 3 nights) — treat prints as provisional · ~35% NW non-SGD (USDSGD 1.2787, USDCNY ≈ 6.70) · ~62% liquid book idle cash

Alpha — signals, not advice

  • HK AI barbell (Asia 10% vs ~3%; AI 15% vs ~1%): entry condition confirmed by the scorecard (SI Dialogue + incident channel = the AI-communique gate, next exchange by Nov 2026). Blocker is price action, not policy: today is the arbiter session — reclaim 439 with volume = tranche trigger; failure toward 425 = wait.
  • Defense sleeve (15% vs ~0%): 10y 5.17% off the peak, 30y 5.50%; both de-escalation tracks live; but PCE Wed + NFP Fri stacked and October ~66%. First-tranche case intact — a half-tranche before PCE is the disciplined version.
  • Silver/miners reload (real assets 20% vs ~4%): 4th defense of the $62–64 zone held (SLV +0.90% → ~$64.3); each prior defense produced a multi-day miner rally; an Iran deal is a direct yield-relief lever. Stagger; watch the 10y at 5.21% as the ceiling tell.

trumpWatch.title: SUMMIT SCORECARD: Beijing publishes eight outcomes — strategic stability, APEC/G20, Iran/Hormuz language, $30bn tariff arrangement, SI Dialogue, pandas
trumpWatch.detail: Post-visit readout (Sep 26): (1) 'strategic stability' relationship framing (respect, fairness, reciprocity); (2) mutual support for China-hosted APEC (Nov) and US-hosted G20 (Dec), both leaders intending to attend each other's; (3) Iran must not develop nuclear weapons + 'no country or institution shall charge transit fees for passage through international waterways'; (4) WWII-allies remembrance; (5) Trade Council ('Board of Trade') + $30bn reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement (US exports: ag, fish/seafood, logs/wood, cosmetics, medical devices; US imports: small appliances, toys, holiday decorations, car seats) + leaders instructed to implement the Kuala Lumpur results; (6) counternarcotics — orphines scheduled, export controls on two fentanyl precursors, 21 August arrests; (7) AI dialogue established — WH-branded 'U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue', next exchange by November 2026, plus a bilateral SI-incident communication channel; (8) pandas to Zoo Atlanta. A mil-mil MoU on crisis communication/prevention is to be signed ASAP.

trumpWatch.title: WH fact sheet extras: China to import at least 10Mt/yr US coal in 2027–28; refined-petroleum ask; rare earths aspirational only
trumpWatch.detail: White House fact sheet adds: China to import at least 10 million metric tons of US coal in 2027 and 2028; Trump urged Xi to increase refined-petroleum production to stabilize global supply; a Board of Investment established; rare earths got only 'continue to work on… ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels' — no binding commitment while shipments fall at the fastest pace since the pandemic; Trump advocated US-Russia-China trilateral arms control.

trumpWatch.title: What did NOT land: Taiwan absent from the eight outcomes; CBS — 'visit wraps up with few achievements announced'
trumpWatch.detail: Taiwan is absent from the outcomes document; the US side held the standard formula: 'He's fully committed to the One China policy. We're committed to the Taiwan Relations Act, the three communiques, and the six assurances.' CBS framed the close as light on achievements. The truce extension to January 10, 2027 (announced Wednesday) remains the hard deliverable.

trumpWatch.title: Iran's Friday proposal: reopen Hormuz + resume nuclear talks within 7 days — WTI −2.33% to $92.41 (−7.4% w/w)
trumpWatch.detail: Tehran's conditions: lift the naval blockade, unfreeze Iranian assets, end the war 'on all fronts' — a sequenced agreement resembling the June MOU that collapsed weeks later. Hormuz flows 33.7M barrels this week, roughly on track with the prior week; speculation the US could restrict diesel exports.

trumpWatch.title: Rates: 10y eased 4bp to 5.17% off the 5.21% peak; October-hike odds ~66%; Bessent buybacks seen as having 'limited impact'
trumpWatch.detail: Hawkish Fed comments collided with UMich's confirmed sharp rise in inflation expectations; TE: Bessent's Treasury-buyback attempts to cap long yields 'widely seen as having had limited impact'; the 30y (5.50%) is still rising. Last week's central banks (Newsquawk Week in Review): Norges HIKED 25bp to 4.50% (hawkish; next seemingly Q2-2027), SNB held 0.00% (inflation forecasts lifted), Riksbank held 1.75% with hawkish forecasts, Banxico outcome not explicitly captured (previews pointed to a 6.50% hold), SARB hiked 25bp to 7.25% Tuesday.

trumpWatch.title: This week's slate: RBA Tuesday (hike ~96% priced), US PCE Wednesday, EZ CPI flash + US NFP Friday
trumpWatch.detail: Mon: BoJ minutes (Jul), China industrial profits (Aug). Tue: RBA decision (~96% priced hike; risk asymmetry in the statement/presser), Spanish inflation, EZ sentiment, Canadian GDP, US JOLTS. Wed: Australian CPI (day AFTER the RBA), China NBS PMI (Sep), US ADP, US GDP final Q2 + US PCE (Aug). Thu: Japan Tankan Q3, US claims, US ISM Manufacturing (exp 55.0 vs 54.6; S&P flash was a 52-month high 57.0). Fri: Tokyo CPI, EZ CPI flash (exp 3.5–3.8% from 3.2%), US NFP (consensus 100k vs 162k prev; U3 4.1%; AHE +0.3% m/m).
